built_from.registry: registry.json (96 conditions, 35 classes; two rows carry sites:2 for the advertised 98)
built_from.codex: codex-sweep.json (13 concerns, attached to their criteria as codex_concern)

criteria.note: Check 61 tests only that a Conformance section exists (md track); populated-vs-placeholder content and the track/stage gating (Standards Track at public-review/CS/OS) are not tested.
No condition scans Non-Standards Track packages for mandatory normative language outside quoted excerpts.
Existence of a Conformance section is tested (check 61, attached to AC-CONTENT-01) but top-level placement, numbered clauses, and cross-revision numbering stability are not.
Clause-level target identification and normative-reference precision are semantic; no condition attempts them.
No condition tests for a References section or normative/informative separation.

checks.sig: has no matching anchor in the HTML

criteria.note: Fragment-link resolution and presence of a linked TOC are tested; literal agreement of TOC entries with actual heading text/numbers is not.
md track only: RFC 2119 citation backing and RFC 8174 pairing are tested; docx track and consistency-of-usage across the body are not. Codex: authorities support SHOULD, not MUST, for consistency.
criteria.codex_concern: The quoted authorities support declaring RFC 2119/BCP 14 usage as a recommendation/checklist item and using keywords consistently, but they do not clearly support a mandatory 'MUST use those key words consistently' requirement. The criterion should likely use SHOULD throughout or cite stronger policy text for the MUST.

criteria.note: No condition tests for 'Non-normative' labels on appendices/examples.
Delivery-format completeness is mechanically enforced (items exist, required formats present, This-stage block lists md/html/pdf).
Presence of an authoritative source artifact is enforced, but the explicit cover-page designation of exactly one authoritative format is not verified.

Editable/authoritative source must travel with the renderings in the package that goes to the repository. Codex: 'alongside the renders' framing is our packaging convention, delivery-to-repository is the policy core.
criteria.codex_concern: The quoted text supports requiring editable formats of all versions to be delivered to the TC document repository, but it does not clearly require them to be present 'alongside the published HTML/PDF renders.'

criteria.note: JSON validity (well-formed-and-valid arm, TCP-012) is tested; standalone-plain-text-file presence for inline normative definitions, and non-JSON languages, are not.

checks.sig: No 'This version' URL block found on the HTML cover
does not contain the canonical this-stage base URL

criteria.note: This-stage presence is enforced on md, HTML cover, and PDF, and the template-section gate covers front matter generally; independent presence checks for the Previous-stage and Latest-stage fields exist only conditionally (89/90 past stage 01) or as URL-format checks. Codex: 'exactly three persistent URIs' overstated given N/A Previous-stage on first publication.
criteria.codex_concern: The criterion states that exactly three persistent URI fields must appear, but the cited Naming Directives text says 'Previous stage' applies 'when applicable,' and first publications may use 'N/A' rather than a persistent URI. The 'exactly three persistent URI fields' formulation is therefore not clearly supported.

criteria.note: Live-site revision collision plus This-stage-URL-points-at-shipped-file make non-reuse operationally tested (requires network).

no Previous-version block with docs.oasis-open.org URLs found on the HTML cover

criteria.note: Presence of a Previous-stage citation past stage 01 is tested on both tracks; that it points at the immediately preceding published instance (or reads N/A on a first publication) is not verified against publication history.

checks.sig: Latest-stage URL must point at the version root
Latest-version URL must point at the version root

criteria.note: Latest-stage URLs are mechanically held to the version root, under the version directory, never stage-pinned, on both tracks.
No condition compares the stage token across the three cover URIs for internal consistency during public review.
Track designation lives in the required template front-matter sections (md only); no direct text check for 'Standards Track Work Product' / 'Non-Standards Track Work Product' on either cover.

Version is enforced in filenames/directories (version-naming class) but nothing tests the TITLE text for the Version identifier. Codex: 'Version <n>' composition is SHOULD; only incorporation is MUST.
criteria.codex_concern: The authority supports a MUST for incorporating the Version identifier into the title, but the specific title composition using 'Version' immediately after the name is stated as SHOULD. Treating the whole criterion as BLOCKER overstates the severity for the SHOULD portion.

criteria.note: No condition tests the title's leading word.
No condition tests hyphen use inside the title; flagged not machine-testable.
No condition tests acronym placement/case in the title.
No trademark screen on the title; flagged not machine-testable.

The template-section gate implies the notices block and the copyright YEAR is synced to the document date, but the presence/wording of the OASIS copyright notice itself is not directly tested. Codex: policy requires the notice, not a specific front-matter position.
criteria.codex_concern: The quoted policy requires inclusion of the OASIS copyright notice, but does not clearly require that it appear specifically in the front matter.

criteria.note: No condition compares the IPR statement to the TC's recorded IPR mode.
No condition distinguishes Technical Report Authors from Committee Note editors on the cover.
Retired tokens are caught in the stage directory name only; filenames, URIs, and cover-page text are not swept for csprd/cnprd/cos. Codex: cover-page scope for 'cos' is thinner in the authorities.
criteria.codex_concern: The authorities clearly prohibit obsolete abbreviations in filenames and URIs, and some quotes mention cover-page use for csprd/cnprd, but they do not clearly support the full scope of 'any filename, directory name, URI, or cover-page text' for all three tokens, especially directory names and cover-page use of cos.

checks.sig: is not a recognized stage token

criteria.note: Stage token is validated against the union of current tokens; track-appropriateness (csd/cs/os/errata only for Standards Track) is not gated.

checks.sig: is not a recognized stage token

criteria.note: Same union-set validation; cnd/cn-only gating for Non-Standards Track packages is not enforced.
Check 0 owns revision-suffix logic, but the registry text ('csd01, never bare csd') does not evidence the os exemption; verify the implementation exempts bare os rather than flagging it.
Two-digit revision on the stage directory and stage suffix on delivery filenames are both mechanically enforced. Codex: policy scopes this to principal filenames/URIs, not every file in the package.
criteria.codex_concern: The quoted text supports use of a lower-case stage abbreviation with revision number for document identifiers/URIs, principal document filenames, and cover-page stage-specific filenames, but it does not clearly support the broader requirement that every stage-specific filename and directory name in the package must end with that component.

checks.sig: does not match the vN.N convention
does not embed the version segment

criteria.note: Version directory convention, filename/directory agreement, and version embedding are all tested.
No allowed-character (alphanumeric/period/hyphen) scan over package names; only the lowercase and junk-file checks brush against it.
No underscore scan on document URIs.
Leading-dot junk files (.DS_Store etc.) are caught; the general leading/trailing/consecutive-punctuation rule is not tested.
The stricter all-lowercase filename rule makes case-only-differing names impossible to pass; any AC-NAMING-10 violation trips check 75.
Lowercase is enforced on every filename and every self-referential URL path, subsuming the stage-abbrev/tc-shortname lowercase mandate.
No trademark screen on filenames; flagged not machine-testable.
OS junk/editor-backup files are caught, but the named forbidden set (index.html, index.htm, *.cgi, .htaccess) is not explicitly tested.

checks.sig: does not embed the version segment

criteria.note: Shared basename across formats, embedded version, stage suffix, and no working tokens together enforce the single-part filename pattern. Codex: identical-stem framing is stricter than the quoted pattern text; retained as the operational reading.
criteria.codex_concern: The quoted text supports the standard filename pattern for single-part work products, but it does not clearly support the added requirement that source/HTML/PDF delivery filenames must have an identical stem with only the extension varying.

criteria.note: No single-extension check on package filenames.
No IANA MIME-type conformance check on extensions.
No cross-release stability check on supporting-artifact filenames (schemas/images without stage tokens).
No multi-part shared-name/version validation.
No partN identifier validation. Codex: authorities allow Project Administration exceptions; keep that in any future implementation.
criteria.codex_concern: The quoted naming-directives text says the structure is required only 'typically' and 'unless otherwise approved by Project Administration.' The criterion states an absolute MUST and does not reflect that exception.

criteria.note: No check requires the -public-review-metadata.html companion file.
No check requires a -comment-resolution-log file. Codex: authorities give the filename pattern; the MUST-include-in-package reading is ours.
criteria.codex_concern: The quoted text clearly supports the filename pattern for a comment resolution log, but does not clearly support that every package that underwent public review MUST include such a file in the package.

criteria.note: URLs are held under docs.oasis-open.org and must carry version+stage segments, but the full path-component order ([tc-shortname]/[WP-abbrev]/...) is not validated. Codex: multi-part/errata exceptions apply to the pattern.
criteria.codex_concern: The naming-directives quote includes an exception for URI references associated with Multi-Part or Approved Errata Work Products. The criterion states the URI pattern as an unconditional MUST and omits those exceptions.

criteria.note: The live-site collision check blocks re-publishing an existing stage; forward, non-skipped progression against the stage history is not otherwise validated.
Checks 64/95 test the reverse direction (cited files must ship); nothing verifies each shipped normative-definition file is referenced from the specification.
Stage-level overwrite is blocked via the live-site collision check; per-file overwrite/rename/removal within an existing tree, and the Latest-alias exception boundary, are not tested.
No META-refresh, duplicate-content, or redirect-alias detection (symlink check 83 covers only self/ancestor loops).
No scan for member-only/Kavi URIs in the text.

Cover stage URLs are forced under docs.oasis-open.org; general third-party-host and access-restriction sweeps are not implemented. Codex: 'never on any third-party host' is broader than the quoted authority.
criteria.codex_concern: The cited text requires official committee resources/copies to be on OASIS-designated facilities and prohibits committees from storing/hosting official documents on non-designated systems. It does not clearly support the broader statement that every published Work Product artifact may reside only on the OASIS Library/docs.oasis-open.org or that it can never appear on any third-party host.

criteria.note: schema-id checks cover JSON $id, not XML namespace name patterns or http/https consistency.
No /ns/-path retrievable-document detection.
The errata stage token is recognized, but sequential /errataNN/ directories and the list-of-corrections instance are not tested.
Manifest sha256 (check 72) proves internal integrity only; no gate compares a COS-submitted package against its submitted state.
